title: Find an impactful EggCC encoding case

questions.prompt: Which speedups should qualify for this goal?
questions.description: The first example removed a load, but measured only compiler wall time and RSS. A new optimization could speed up the compiled program even if compilation gets slower. Keep compiler/analysis costs and generated-program runtime as separate results.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Either a compiler/analysis speedup or a generated-program speedup can qualify, with a fair equivalent control, validated outputs and repeated measurements; a genuine baseline bug can also qualify.

questions.prompt: When may the search finish without a verified speedup or bug?
questions.description: This follow-on should search more broadly and should not stop merely after another neutral toy example. We will preserve failed and neutral experiments, favor existing EggCC/Bril workloads, and use scalable examples only with a clear connection to a real compiler consumer.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Allow a negative conclusion only after a reviewed candidate map and substantial targeted experiments show why the plausible high-value leads did not yield an impact; otherwise keep pursuing promising leads. Do not impose an arbitrary two-prototype limit.
